summary: The bad() method is a classic logic time bomb (CWE-511): a hidden random trigger that, when SecureRandom.nextInt() happens to equal 20000, launches an attacker-planted executable (evil.exe) via Runtime.exec. There is no legitimate feature embedded here—the entire conditional payload IS the malicious logic. The repair removes the time-bomb trigger and the command execution while leaving the method structurally intact, matching the benign no-op behavior of good().
